fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents present the strongest genuine overlap: CI ownership, automated test environments, measurable improvements, documentation and personal infrastructure projects. They are particularly careful not to convert namespace-level work into cluster administration or personal Terraform/AWS learning into professional cloud experience. Terragrunt, mTLS, production cloud ownership and manufacturer-facing architecture remain substantial gaps; the letter does not directly address the mismatch between this independent contractor remit and the candidate's junior/mid transition.

issues: Considerable repetition between the summary, Odrava experience and selected projects adds length without proportionate new evidence.
The most directly relevant personal Terraform/TLS project follows the less role-specific flaky-test dashboard.
The long headline and current-role heading wrap awkwardly, although both remain readable.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in a sensible order, with intact words and conventional headings.
Certificate management is represented semantically by cert-manager, and virtual machines by the personal VPS; neither establishes broad experience in those areas.
Terraform and AWS are present but explicitly limited to personal projects and basic learning.
Terragrunt, mTLS and production cloud architecture are missing, and the current title remains QA rather than infrastructure engineering.
Java test automation is not equivalent to the requested backend/JVM background.

issues: The first paragraph repeats the career transition and infrastructure positioning rather than quickly establishing the strongest evidence.
Onboarding documentation is mentioned in consecutive sentences.
The Prometheus, Grafana and Loki setup is described in consecutive sentences.
Company-specific content is accurate but relatively light: fleet connectivity and an engineering-led team.
The letter does not directly discuss the absent Terragrunt/mTLS experience or how the candidate would approach the role's independent architecture and stakeholder responsibilities.
strengths: Names the correct company and exact contractor role.
Uses concrete pipeline-time and cost results rather than generic claims.
Clearly distinguishes personal Terraform experience from professional work.
Uses documentation and mentoring as credible communication evidence.
Does not reuse the earlier letter's old employer context or outdated learning statements.

statements_in_outputs: I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role.
culture_used: “Corvale’s engineering-led team” reflects the company information describing it as engineering-led.

spacing_issues: CV page one is dense, while page two is only 40.9% filled and has a large lower blank area.
The CV headline wraps onto a second line with “Platform Engineering” isolated.
The current-role heading wraps “Present” onto its own line.
Long cover-letter paragraphs make the repeated material more noticeable.
issues: The serif type, restrained headings and single-column structure are professional and consistent across the set.
The 10-point CV body is readable but compact; reducing duplication could allow more balanced spacing.
The cover-letter image is clean and uncropped. Its generous lower whitespace is acceptable for a one-page letter.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure” repeats the infrastructure concept within the same summary sentence.
“as well as writing documentation that supports onboarding. I also documented the CI workflow for onboarding” is unnecessarily repetitive.
“monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki” is immediately repeated by “I configured Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring”.

notes_facts_used: Namespace-level access and the platform team's responsibility for cluster administration.
Internal CI documentation used in onboarding.
Basic EC2 and S3 learning through the AWS free tier.
ISTQB Foundation Level certification obtained in 2019.
notes_facts_ignored: CKA study and January 2027 exam booking, explicitly not yet passed.
Observation of two incident calls, with no production on-call experience.
Willingness to target junior/mid DevOps or platform roles and accept a junior title; this could inform honest discussion of the seniority mismatch, although advertising a title drop is not necessary.

evaluation.summary: These are credible, well-grounded documents that present the candidate's CI/CD and test-infrastructure achievements without inflating personal cloud work into professional experience. The CV follows the requested experience ordering and has an exactly two-sentence summary, while both PDFs are readable and parse cleanly. The application remains a stretch for an independent cloud-infrastructure contractor role because strong Terragrunt, mTLS, production cloud architecture and manufacturer-facing technical leadership are not evidenced. Repeated content, uneven CV page density and omission of accurately labelled CKA preparation are the main avoidable weaknesses.
